title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: The write count next to a state only looks at the file it is in. For a private backing field that is the whole truth. For a property anyone can reach, it is not, and the lens still read 0 writes flatly.

highlights.title: The count says its scope
highlights.description: A state that is not private now reads 0 writes in this file, the same reservation the reader count has carried all along.

highlights.title: Three real cases
highlights.description: Of 21 non private states with no write in their own file, 3 are written elsewhere, one of them in four other files.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A private state keeps the plain wording: nothing outside the file can write it, so the count is complete.
The reservation sits next to the number, ahead of the indirect writer note, so both stay readable.
